title: Everyone remembers the miracle.
paragraphs: Everyone remembers the miracle.

Five loaves.
Two fish.
Five thousand people fed.
But hidden inside this famous story is a quiet detail many people overlook.
The miracle began with a boy.
In a crowd of thousands of adults, only one person is recorded as offering something.
A child.
His lunch wasn’t impressive.

Five small barley loaves were the food of the poor.
Two fish were barely enough for a family meal.
And yet somehow, that small basket became the starting point of a miracle that fed a multitude.
Think about the moment.
The disciples were calculating the problem.
“How far will this go among so many?”
But the boy wasn’t calculating.
He was surrendering.
He gave what looked too small to matter.
And when it entered the hands of Jesus, something extraordinary happened.
Because God does not require abundance.
He requires surrender.
Many people are waiting for God to give them more before they act.

More resources.
More clarity.
More confidence.
More time.
But heaven often multiplies what is released, not what is stored.
The miracle of the feeding of the 5,000 teaches us something profound:
God can feed thousands with what we think is not enough.
But the miracle never begins until something is placed in His hands.
And the boy who gave away his lunch probably never imagined that his small act of surrender would become one of the most famous miracles in Scripture.
Sometimes the smallest offering becomes the doorway to the largest miracle.
